title: Operational
description: Celery queue depth + task success rate + batch flakiness. Trend-shape window — operational issues compound over hours.

panels.title: Celery task rate by name (tasks/min)
panels.description: Per-task completion rate. Drift signals a beat schedule misalignment or a queue backlog.

panels.title: Celery task success rate by name
panels.description: Success / total ratio per task. Below 0.9 sustained = investigate.

panels.title: Celery task error rate by name
panels.description: Error rate per task. Outcome label = 'error'. Alert source for D19.2.

panels.title: Celery retry rate by name
panels.description: Retry events per task. Spike = transient downstream failure (Redis, LLM, external).

panels.title: Memory recall hit rate
panels.description: Recalled rows per second by mode (semantic / lexical). Low hit rate suggests embeddings drift or DB index regression.

panels.title: Memory write rate
panels.description: Memories written per second by scope. Sudden zero = consumer drift; sudden spike = unbounded write loop.

panels.title: Tool call p95 latency by tool (seconds)
panels.description: p95 latency for each registered tool. Tool latency dominates agent-invocation latency for tool-heavy specialists.

notes: D18 Phase B closure documented batch-flakiness under real-LLM load (~1-3 transient flakes per full-suite run). D19.1 CP3 closure surfaced 2 additional batch-flake instances (see docs/followups/cp3-traceability-supervisor-flake.md). The split between 'rate-limit retry' and 'contract failure' (per D-A operational note) lives in logs / spans — log query on event='agent.run.error' grouped by error_type. Surface as a dashboard placeholder rather than ship a wrong metric.
